bib.title: Smarter, Better, Faster, Longer: A Modern Bidirectional Encoder for Fast, Memory Efficient, and Long Context Finetuning and Inference

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only for lineage.

question: Can modern LLM-era architecture, data scale and hardware-aware design yield an encoder-only model that beats BERT-era encoders on retrieval, classification and code while being faster and more memory efficient, with 8192-token context?
hypothesis: Encoders benefit from both recent pretraining data scales and architecture improvements from autoregressive LLMs.
contributions: ModernBERT-base (149M) and -large (395M), trained on 2T tokens with 8192 native context
FlexBERT modular architecture framework and all intermediate training checkpoints released
State-of-the-art encoder results on GLUE, BEIR (DPR and ColBERT), MLDR, code retrieval
Best encoder inference speed and memory efficiency on common GPUs

method.summary: Encoder-only transformer with RoPE, GeGLU, pre-norm, alternating global/local attention, full unpadding, trained with MLM (30% mask) on 2T tokens (1.719T at 1024 + 300B context extension to 8192). Evaluated by fine-tuning each backbone (and baselines) on GLUE, MS MARCO retrieval (DPR and ColBERT), MLDR and CoIR code tasks, plus synthetic inference throughput on an RTX 4090.
method.task: masked language model pretraining; downstream retrieval, NLU, code retrieval

datasets.name: ModernBERT pretraining mixture
datasets.source: primarily English web documents, code, scientific literature; exact sources not listed
datasets.preprocessing: sequence packing, greedy, >99% efficiency; context-extension phase 2 upsamples higher-quality sources

datasets.name: BEIR
datasets.preprocessing: LR chosen on NFCorpus, SciFact, TREC-Covid, FiQA

datasets.name: MLDR (English)
datasets.split: OOD: no MLDR training; ID: fine-tuned on MLDR train

datasets.name: CodeSearchNet and StackOverflow-QA
datasets.size: StackQA queries ~1,400 words, docs ~1,200 words (>2000 tokens)

models.name: ModernBERT-base
models.architecture: encoder-only, 22 layers, GeGLU, RoPE, pre-norm, alternating attention

models.name: ModernBERT-large
models.init_from: ModernBERT-base weights via center tiling with wraparound and Gopher layer scaling

models.name: BERT, RoBERTa, DeBERTaV3, NomicBERT, GTE-en-MLM (base and large where exist)

other.use: teacher scores for ColBERT KL distillation

training.objective: MLM, 30% masking, no NSP; fine-tuning: contrastive (DPR), KL distillation (ColBERT)
training.lr: base 8e-4 (pretrain), 3e-4 (context ext.); large 5e-4 then 5e-5 after rollback; ext. large 5e-5
training.lr_schedule: modified trapezoidal (warmup-stable-decay) with 1-sqrt decay; decay 50B tokens in context-extension phase two
training.warmup: base 3B tokens LR warmup; large 2B tokens; batch-size warmup base 768 to 4,608 over 50B tokens, large 448 to 4,928 over 10B tokens
training.tokens: 2T total: 1.719T at seq 1024 + 250B (phase one, 8192) + 50B (phase two decay)
training.weight_decay: 1e-5 (base), 1e-5 then 1e-6 after rollback (large); fully decoupled, none on bias/norm
training.regularisation: StableAdamW update clipping instead of gradient clipping
training.wall_clock: Table 3 total hours: pretraining base 194.2 / large 425.3; phase one 39.9 / 80.7; phase two 11.5 / 21.7 (column-to-model mapping inferred from table order)

other.software: PyTorch 2.4.0, Cuda 12.4.0, Composer 0.24.1, Flash Attention 2.6.3, FA3 commit 32792d3
other.final checkpoint: base: average of 3 best annealing checkpoints plus final; large: best annealing checkpoint
other.fine-tune ColBERT: batch 16, 5% LR warmup, JaColBERTv2.5 recipe, PyLate
other.BEIR LR sweep: [1e-5, 2e-5, 3e-5, 5e-5, 8e-5, 1e-4]; chosen ModernBERT DPR 8e-5 base / 1e-4 large, ColBERT 1e-4 base / 3e-5 large (Table 9)
other.GLUE sweep: LR [1e-5,3e-5,5e-5,8e-5], WD [1e-6,5e-6,8e-6,1e-5], epochs [1,2,3] or [2,5,10]; early stopping; RTE/MRPC/STS-B start from MNLI checkpoint
other.live eval: MNLI plus validation loss on 500 million randomly sampled sequences

inference.retrieval: DPR: single vector, cosine similarity; ColBERT: MaxSim over token vectors

limits: English only; trained largely on web data so inherits its biases.
MLM-only objective; DeBERTaV3 strength on classification suggests MLM+RTD might do better.
Only data scaling explored; model-parameter scaling left unexplored.
Authors do not explain why ModernBERT trails GTE-en-MLM in long-context single-vector OOD; hypotheses (local attention, GTE's longer-sequence compute) untested.
Single run per cell, no seeds or significance tests; BEIR average driven by TREC-COVID.
GTE-en-MLM GLUE numbers taken from its paper because the authors' own sweep was inconsistent.
Efficiency measured on one RTX 4090 with synthetic data only.
Backbone, not an embedder: retrieval numbers depend on authors' MS MARCO fine-tuning recipe.
